title: Suction (vacuum) cleaning of floors and carpets
audience: Trained cleaners who vacuum carpets, hard floors and entry mats in any cleaning-group business.
learningOutcomes: Complete the pre-use check on a vacuum, covering the bag, filter, hose and beater bar height.
Remove large debris by hand, wearing gloves, before vacuuming.
Vacuum the edges first, then the middle in overlapping passes, working back toward the exit.
Work busy traffic areas with the pile and then against it, to lift the pile.
Keep barrier mats clean at the surface, at the edges and in the mat well.
Empty, clean and store the vacuum and tools after use.

instruction.heading: Why vacuuming needs its own checks
instruction.body: A vacuum combines electricity, moving air and a hose that can block. A blocked filter makes the motor overheat, and a beater bar set at the wrong height leaves carpet pile uneven or fails to lift dirt. A vacuum is also a dust generator, so the way it is used, and the condition of its bag and filter, matter for the people who breathe the air afterwards. The source treats vacuum checks as part of the electrical equipment routine, and requires that only trained employees use electrical equipment.

instruction.heading: The pre-use check
instruction.body: Check the test label, the plug, and the flex for damage, bare wires and tape. Check the bag and filter: a full bag or a blocked filter reduces suction and causes overheating. Look through the hose for any blockage, and clear it with the correct tool rather than with your hand. Set the beater bar height for the carpet pile or floor you are working on. Record what you found.

instruction.heading: Clearing debris and managing the cable
instruction.body: Put on gloves before you pick anything up. Remove large items by hand and place them in a bin bag. Run the cable behind you, so you cannot trip over it or catch the vacuum on it. Connect only after the socket is switched off, and switch the socket off before you unplug. Wear gloves and eye protection when you handle the bag and filter, because dust and bacteria are present.

instruction.heading: Vacuum pattern and busy areas
instruction.body: Vacuum the outside edges of the room first, then work the middle in overlapping passes, moving back toward the exit. In doorways and other busy traffic areas, vacuum with the pile and then against it, which lifts the pile and draws out dirt that a single pass leaves behind. Once the floor is complete, check the edges for any build-up of dirt.

instruction.heading: Barrier mats and care after use
instruction.body: Where barrier mats are fitted, fixed or leased, they are kept clean: no dirt on the surface, around the edges, or underneath in the mat well. This applies only where barrier mats are fitted. After use, switch off the socket, unplug, safety check and damp wipe the vacuum, and dispose of the rubbish. Clean the dust pan and brush, and store them by colour.

procedure: Complete the pre-use check on the vacuum, including the bag, filter, hose and beater bar, and record it.
Put on gloves and eye protection. Remove large debris by hand into a bin bag.
Confirm the socket is off, plug in, and run the cable behind you.
Vacuum the outside edges first, then the middle in overlapping passes, working back toward the exit.
In busy areas, vacuum with the pile and then against it.
Check and clean any barrier mat, including its edges and mat well.
Switch off the socket and unplug. Safety check and damp wipe the vacuum, and empty or replace the bag as needed.
Dispose of the rubbish, clean the dust pan and brush, store them by colour, and record any defect.

workedExamples.situation: The entrance carpet has grit throughout, and the vacuum starts to smell hot partway through the job.
workedExamples.reasoning: Switch the socket off and unplug. Check the bag and filter for a blockage, because a hot smell suggests overheating. Do not carry on with a hot machine. Empty or replace the bag and clear the filter as the manufacturer directs. If the machine still runs hot, tag it as faulty and report it.

workedExamples.situation: A fixed barrier mat in a lobby has dirt packed under its edge, and the vacuum head is set too high to pick it up.
workedExamples.reasoning: Lower the beater bar to suit the mat and the surface, then vacuum the mat edges and the mat well. Remove any caked dirt by the approved method before vacuuming the floor around the mat. Record the condition of the mat, because a dirty mat well is often a recurring issue.

equipmentAndPpe: Vacuum with a current test label.
Spare bags and filters that match the machine.
Gloves for handling debris, bags and filters.
Eye protection when dust is visible.

commonErrors.error: Vacuuming with a blocked filter until the machine overheats.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the bag, filter and hose before switching on. Stop at the first hot smell.

commonErrors.error: Letting the cable run under the vacuum.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep the cable behind you and in view at all times.

commonErrors.error: Setting the beater bar too high or too low for the pile.
commonErrors.prevention: Adjust the beater bar for the surface before you start.

commonErrors.error: Skipping the edges of barrier mats and the mat well.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the mat surface, edges and mat well on every visit where a mat is fitted.

commonErrors.error: Handling a bag or filter without gloves.
commonErrors.prevention: Gloves on before the bag or filter is touched.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Electrical test and tag requirements are set out in “Safe use and care of electrical machines”.
Check the SDS for any product used with the vacuum.
Only trained people use electrical equipment, as the source requires.
Trip hazard: keep the cable behind the operator and out of walkways.

qualityStandard: Pre-use check completed, covering bag, filter, hose and beater bar, and recorded.
Edges vacuumed first, then the middle in overlapping passes toward the exit.
Busy traffic areas worked with the pile and then against it.
Barrier mats free of dirt on the surface, around the edges and in the mat well.
No hot, damaged or untested machine used.
documentationEvidence: Pre-use check record for the vacuum, with any defect found.
Defect report for any machine that is faulty, hot or damaged.
Barrier mat condition record where a mat is fitted.
summary: Check the bag, filter, hose, beater bar and flex before every use.
Edges first, then overlapping passes back toward the exit.
Busy areas get a pass with the pile and a pass against it.
A hot smell means stop, unplug and check. Barrier mats are cleaned at surface, edges and mat well.

knowledgeChecks.question: Before you vacuum, what do you check on the bag and filter?
options: Nothing, as long as the machine starts and the bag looks fine by eye today
Whether the bag is full and the filter is clear, because a blockage causes overheating
Only the colour of the bag and the make of the machine used on this site today

knowledgeChecks.question: In a busy doorway, what is the correct technique?
options: One pass only, then move on and check the result later
Vacuum only diagonally across the doorway at a steady pace
Vacuum with the pile, then against the pile to lift it

knowledgeChecks.question: A vacuum starts to smell hot during a job. What is the right action?
options: Keep going, because the smell will pass once the machine has warmed up for the whole day
Switch the socket off, unplug, check the bag and filter, and report it if the problem continues
Spray air freshener into the bag and close the lid, then carry on with the job until it is finished
